survivingClaim: Precise obstruction for the routes examined. On the Eisenstein channel T_p = U(log p) + U(-log p) = 2 cos(log p sqrt(-L)) (classical fact restated); its compression to K is Z(log p) + Z(log p)^*, of energy norm at most 2 for every inner scattering function (relative to the classical Lax-Phillips identification), and resonance states are not its eigenvectors; in the weighted-L2 family admissibility of the resonance state already implies the eigenvalue bound; on finite spans a norm bound for all p is equivalent to resonance location; no positive-definite form makes T_2 and T_3 both symmetric on a resonance state. Not closed: norms outside the one weight family and infinite-dimensional independent derivations of a norm bound. No statement about zeros of zeta.

lesson: On the continuous spectrum of PSL(2,Z)\H the Hecke operator equals 2 cos(log p sqrt(-L)), so it adds nothing to the Lax-Phillips semigroup; all arithmetic sits inside phi, and the operator framework is identical for every inner function, including non-arithmetic groups and moved resonances. Any Hecke norm bound on resonance states is either implied by admissibility (weighted L2) or equivalent to resonance location. The truncation-Hecke defect lives on the window (a/p, a) and is the automorphic form of closed row G25.
